# CodexMeter 1.4.5
A maintenance release following a full security and code-quality review of the project.
## What changed
- **Security and technical review.** Process execution, SQL construction, Keychain storage, login-file handling, network TLS/redirect behavior, Sparkle update verification, CI supply chain, diagnostics logging, and dependency currency were all reviewed. No security issues were found — the project's existing defenses (sandboxed subprocess environments, code-signature checks before executing the Codex app-server, TOCTOU-safe file access, redirect rejection on the profile API, Sparkle 2.9.6 already current) held up. - **Zero compiler warnings.** Fixed the one remaining warning in the project: `SettingsToggleRow` forwarded its get/set closures into a SwiftUI `Binding` initializer that only infers Sendable safety for closure literals written at the call site, not forwarded parameters. `swift build` now completes cleanly.
No preference, control, or user-visible behavior changed.
## Verification
- 283 automated tests, 0 failures (7 environment-integration tests skipped). - `swift build` with zero warnings and zero errors. - Universal 2 build for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later; the bundled Claude limits helper is signed and verified as part of the release. - The app remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-notarized. SHA-256 protects the first download; Sparkle authenticates later update feeds and archives with Ed25519 signatures.
## Install or update with Homebrew
```bash brew update brew upgrade --cask --greedy HechoLP/tap/codexmeter ```
For a new installation:
```bash brew install --cask HechoLP/tap/codexmeter ```
If macOS blocks this certificate-free app after installation, confirm that it came from `HechoLP/tap/codexmeter`, then remove quarantine from this app only:
```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CodexMeter.app open /Applications/CodexMeter.app ```
## First direct-download launch
Download `CodexMeter-1.4.5.dmg` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` from this release into the same folder. Verify the checksum before opening the disk image:
```bash cd ~/Downloads grep ' CodexMeter-1.4.5.dmg$' SHA256SUMS.txt | shasum -a 256 -c - open CodexMeter-1.4.5.dmg ```
Only after the checksum reports `OK`, copy `CodexMeter.app` to Applications and use the app-scoped quarantine command above.
## Recovery
This release does not migrate any database. Published version tags are immutable; corrections ship as a new patch release.
